Post Run Drip · design prototype

Signals, without a score

The recovery score is gone. What replaces it: what moved first, then one row per variable measured against that athlete’s own usual range — none of them added together. A single number over these four cancels them, which is exactly why the old one never moved in seven months.

What you’re looking at

Every figure is real, from training_logs, daily_biometrics and body_mentions. Baselines are the 28 days sitting behind this window, so each variable is measured against that athlete’s own normal rather than a population constant. A night with no reading draws a gap, never a zero.

Nothing here is a verdict. Both directions are drawn identically and in graphite — a resting HR above your usual is not “bad”, it is above your usual, and one night cannot separate fatigue from a late meal, a warm room or the start of a cold. The screen reports the measurement and the range it normally sits in; the reader draws the line.

Built on the locked system: colors_and_type.css tokens, the four font roles inlined, red reserved for alert, and the 2px leading-edge rule used for mood and nothing else — which is why what moved takes a heavy ink rule at the top instead.
